steps.title: Check Responsiveness
steps.instruction: Shake the person gently and shout 'Are you okay?' Check if they respond.
steps.warning: Do not shake if you suspect spinal injury

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.instruction: Call 911 (or local emergency number) immediately. Ask someone nearby to find an AED if available.
steps.warning: Stay on the line with emergency services

steps.title: Position the Person
steps.instruction: Place the person on their back on a firm surface. Tilt their head back slightly by lifting the chin.
steps.warning: Ensure airway is clear

steps.title: Hand Placement
steps.instruction: Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest between the nipples. Place your other hand on top, interlocking fingers.
steps.warning: Keep arms straight and shoulders directly over hands

steps.title: Start Chest Compressions
steps.instruction: Push hard and fast at least 2 inches deep. Compress at 100-120 beats per minute. Count: 1, 2, 3... up to 30.
steps.warning: Allow complete chest recoil between compressions

steps.title: Rescue Breaths
steps.instruction: Tilt head back, lift chin. Pinch nose shut. Cover their mouth with your mouth and give 2 breaths, each lasting 1 second.
steps.warning: Watch for chest rise with each breath

steps.title: Continue CPR
steps.instruction: Continue cycles of 30 chest compressions and 2 rescue breaths until emergency services arrive or the person starts breathing normally.
steps.warning: Do not stop CPR unless person shows signs of life

steps.title: Assess the Situation
steps.instruction: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they can speak or cough forcefully, encourage continued coughing.
steps.warning: If they cannot speak, cough, or breathe, act immediately

steps.title: Call for Help
steps.instruction: Call 911 immediately or have someone else call while you provide aid.
steps.warning: Time is critical - don't delay treatment

steps.title: Back Blows
steps.instruction: Stand behind the person. Lean them forward and give 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
steps.warning: Support their chest while giving back blows

steps.title: Abdominal Thrusts
steps.instruction: Stand behind person, wrap arms around waist. Place fist above navel, grasp with other hand. Give 5 quick upward thrusts.
steps.warning: Do not perform on pregnant women or infants

steps.title: Alternate and Repeat
steps.instruction: Continue alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or person becomes unconscious.
steps.warning: If person becomes unconscious, begin CPR

steps.title: Ensure Safety
steps.instruction: Put on gloves if available. Ensure the scene is safe for you and the injured person.
steps.warning: Protect yourself from bloodborne pathogens

steps.title: Apply Direct Pressure
steps.instruction: Place a clean cloth or sterile gauze directly on the wound. Apply firm, steady pressure with your hands.
steps.warning: Do not remove cloth if it becomes soaked - add more layers

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.instruction: Call 911 if bleeding is severe, won't stop after 10 minutes, or if you see signs of shock.
steps.warning: Describe the severity and location of the bleeding

steps.title: Elevate if Possible
steps.instruction: If no broken bones are suspected, raise the injured area above the level of the heart while maintaining pressure.
steps.warning: Do not elevate if it causes more pain or you suspect fracture

steps.title: Monitor for Shock
steps.instruction: Watch for pale skin, rapid breathing, weakness. Keep person lying down and cover with blanket to maintain body temperature.
steps.warning: Signs of shock require immediate emergency care

steps.title: Ensure Safety
steps.instruction: Remove the person from the source of the burn. Turn off electricity, extinguish flames, or move away from chemicals.
steps.warning: Do not put yourself at risk

steps.title: Assess Severity
steps.instruction: Check the size and depth of burn. Call 911 for large burns (larger than palm), burns on face/hands/feet/genitals, or third-degree burns.
steps.warning: When in doubt, seek professional medical help

steps.title: Cool the Burn
steps.instruction: Run cool (not cold) water over the burn for 10-20 minutes. Remove jewelry/clothing before swelling begins.
steps.warning: Do not use ice, butter, or oils on burns

steps.title: Protect the Area
steps.instruction: Cover with a sterile, non-adhesive bandage or clean cloth. Do not break blisters if they form.
steps.warning: Avoid cotton balls or fluffy materials that can stick

steps.title: Monitor and Treat Pain
steps.instruction: Give over-the-counter pain medication as needed. Watch for signs of infection: increased pain, fever, drainage, or red streaking.
steps.warning: Seek medical attention if signs of infection develop

steps.title: Check Responsiveness
steps.instruction: Gently shake the person's shoulders and call their name loudly. Check if they respond to voice or touch.
steps.warning: Do not shake vigorously if you suspect head or neck injury

steps.title: Position Safely
steps.instruction: If breathing normally, place in recovery position (on their side). If not breathing normally, prepare for CPR.
steps.warning: Check for normal breathing - look, listen, feel

steps.title: Call for Help
steps.instruction: Call 911 if person doesn't wake up within 1 minute, has difficulty breathing, or you're concerned about their condition.
steps.warning: Better to call emergency services unnecessarily than to wait too long

steps.title: Elevate Legs
steps.instruction: If person is breathing and conscious but weak, have them lie down and elevate legs 8-12 inches above heart level.
steps.warning: Only if no suspected spinal injury

steps.title: Monitor Vital Signs
steps.instruction: Stay with the person, monitor breathing and consciousness. Loosen tight clothing around neck and waist.
steps.warning: Be prepared to start CPR if breathing stops

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.instruction: Call 911 immediately if person has difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, or widespread rash.
steps.warning: Anaphylaxis can be life-threatening within minutes

steps.title: Use Epinephrine
steps.instruction: If person has an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen), help them use it immediately into the outer thigh.
steps.warning: Remove safety cap and press firmly against thigh for 10 seconds

steps.title: Keep Person Calm
steps.instruction: Have person sit up if breathing is difficult, or lie down if feeling faint. Remove or avoid the allergen if known.
steps.warning: Do not leave person alone

steps.title: Monitor Breathing
steps.instruction: Watch for signs of worsening: increased difficulty breathing, loss of consciousness, or severe drop in blood pressure.
steps.warning: Be prepared to perform CPR if person becomes unresponsive

steps.title: Prepare for Second Dose
steps.instruction: If symptoms don't improve or worsen after 5-15 minutes, give second epinephrine dose if available.
steps.warning: Continue monitoring until emergency medical help arrives

disclaimer: Sahaaya provides first-aid guidance based on recognized medical standards. This app is not a substitute for professional medical care. Always call emergency services for serious medical emergencies. The information provided should not replace proper first-aid training.
